log.hypothesis: Baseline of the unedited model: all side-effect metrics should be at their reference values; soft1e-4 should show a large response ratio relative to split2/soft3e-3 because a 0.06 GeV photon is far outside the neutral pT range.

The response to one added photon peaks near pT fraction 1e-3 (log pT ~ -0.5), a narrow band, suggesting a localized detector rather than generic IR sensitivity; neutral hadrons may behave differently. Summary-token change should appear at a specific depth.

The summary-token change for a sub-threshold photon is absent at block5 and large at body.norm; I expect it to switch on abruptly in one block between 6 and 11 (a localized detector), with the soft-photon token itself diverging from the 3e-3 control first.

The soft-photon detector feature read by block-7 heads 0/5 is written by a small set of MLP units in blocks 0-6 that fire selectively on sub-threshold neutral tokens; their per-unit contribution to the head-0 summary logit will be concentrated in a few units.

Statistics capture: detector units (block5 u266, block6 u294/470/275) have pre-activations well separated between sub-threshold photons and all normal tokens (clean, P, D, J), so a bias shift can make them exact gates; normal-token residual covariances at blocks 6-10 and body.norm give >100 sigma readout of a saturated gate pattern.

Zeroing the output scale of 11 selective soft-neutral detector units (blocks 4-7) removes about 40% of the block-7 head-0 sink logit, so the soft1e-3 response drops by roughly half while clean metrics barely move (these units are ~constant small negative on normal tokens).

Statistics capture for the classifier block-1 queries (summary tokens after classifier block 0) so that a rank-1 key edit can suppress gated tokens in both classifier attention blocks; summary-token queries per head should share a common direction (projection >0 for >95% of queries).

Block-6 unit 294 turned into a sharp gate writes a saturating sign pattern into sub-threshold neutral tokens; rank-1 key edits in body blocks 7-11 and both classifier blocks read that pattern and push the gated key ~12 logits down for every query, removing the token from all attention after block 6. Residual error is the natural influence in blocks 0-6.
Keys-only part of T2 (no gate, so no token is ever suppressed): isolates the side effect of the readout noise on normal keys.

Gate-only part of T2: sub-threshold neutral tokens get a saturated residual but are not suppressed; isolates the gate's effect (expected large response to soft photons and the main source of gen_drift).

Flag-channel removal: channel 450 is pushed to -20 for all tokens at block 6 (saturated, constant after every later DyT), gate unit 294 flips it to ~+80 on sub-threshold neutrals, and column-450 key edits in body blocks 7-11 and both classifier blocks lower the flagged key by >=12 logits for 95% of queries. No readout noise on normal tokens, so clean metrics should stay near T1 levels while soft responses drop like T2.

Moving the flag one block earlier (bias shift and gate u266 in block 5, u294 kept as a second OR gate, suppression in blocks 6-11 + classifier) removes the soft token's influence in block 6 too; soft1e-4 should improve modestly, clean stays clean.

Flag gate (3 DoF) plus suppression only in block-7 heads 0 and 5 (64 entries): removes the head-0 summary sink and the head-5 particle sink that carry most of the flaw, leaving natural attention elsewhere.
Flag gate plus all 16 heads of block 7: the flagged token disappears from block-7 attention entirely; later blocks still see it (block 9 h0, block 10 h13 had elevated attention).

Flag gate plus suppression in body blocks 7-11 but not in the classifier: the classifier still attends to the flagged token's body.norm output, so a residual leak remains compared with the full flag edit.

Same two-gate flag removal as pass 15 but each head's suppression direction restricted to the few head coordinates whose query signs are consistent (q05 >= 0.3 median): flag is binary so larger gamma costs nothing; expect identical soft ratios at ~1/8 of the DoF.
Sparse version of the single-gate flag edit (pass 14): same behaviour at DoF 414.
Sparse two-gate flag with the tail criterion q01 >= 0.3 median and gamma set at q01 (99% of queries suppressed by >=12 logits): should recover most of the dense result.
Same with q01 >= 0.5 median: closer to dense suppression.
